reason: The text features multiple regular people characters with clear lines, emotions, and agency. Moses speaks directly ('וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה כֹּה אָמַר יְהוָה' - 'And Moses said, Thus says the LORD'), conveying God's message and leading the Israelites. Pharaoh appears as a character with direct speech and emotional urgency, calling out to Moses and Aaron at night and commanding them to leave ('וַיִּקְרָא לְמֹשֶׁה וּלְאַהֲרֹן לַיְלָה וַיֹּאמֶר ק֤וּמוּ צְּאוּ֙'). The Egyptians are portrayed with clear emotional reactions—fear and desperation that compels them to urgently release the Israelites ('וַתֶּחֱזַק מִצְרַיִם עַל־ הָעָם... כִּי אָמְרוּ כֻּלָּנוּ מֵתִים' - 'Egypt pressed the people... saying "We are all dying"'). The Israelites are shown taking deliberate action following Moses' instructions. These are not merely passive subjects but characters with agency, speech, and emotional responses.
